heading_path: 197  Powers of Federal Court and Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) on hearing an appeal
text: On hearing an appeal against a decision or direction of the Registrar, the Federal Court or the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) may do any one or more of the following: (a) admit evidence orally, or on affidavit or otherwise; (b) permit the examination and crossexamination of witnesses, including witnesses who gave evidence before the Registrar; (c) order an issue of fact to be tried as it directs; (d) affirm, reverse or vary the Registrar’s decision or direction; (e) give any judgment, or make any order, that, in all the circumstances, it thinks fit; (f) order a party to pay costs to another party.
title: Powers of Federal Court and Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) on hearing an appeal

units.text: On hearing an appeal against a decision or direction of the Registrar, the Federal Court or the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2) may do any one or more of the following:
(a) admit evidence orally, or on affidavit or otherwise;
(b) permit the examination and crossexamination of witnesses, including witnesses who gave evidence before the Registrar;
(c) order an issue of fact to be tried as it directs;
(d) affirm, reverse or vary the Registrar’s decision or direction;
(e) give any judgment, or make any order, that, in all the circumstances, it thinks fit;
(f) order a party to pay costs to another party.
